**Observation Log:**

[FACT] User is considering scheduling a maintenance check for their road bike at the local bike shop.  
[EVENT] User decided to upgrade their road bike's pedals to Shimano Ultegra clipless pedals today.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant congratulated the user on their decision to upgrade to clipless pedals and provided a step-by-step guide for installing Shimano Ultegra pedals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Tools needed for installation include Shimano Ultegra pedals, a pedal wrench, and optional grease.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Pre-installation checks include checking pedal compatibility and preparing clipless shoes compatible with Shimano SPD-SL pedals.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Installation steps include removing old pedals, inspecting and cleaning the crankset, applying grease, installing new pedals, tightening them, and checking their security.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Setting up shoes and pedals involves attaching cleats, adjusting cleat position, and practicing clipping in and out.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Final checks include double-checking pedal security and taking a test ride.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant advised that if the user is uncomfortable with the installation process, they should consider taking the bike to a local bike shop for professional assistance.  
[FACT] User is concerned about the brakes on their road bike feeling spongy lately.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided possible causes for spongy brakes, including air in the system, worn or damaged brake pads, contaminated brake pads, misaligned brake caliper, and cable stretch or wear.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Potential solutions for spongy brakes include adjusting the brakes, replacing brake pads, replacing brake cables, or replacing the brake caliper or lever.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended having the mechanic inspect the brake system during the maintenance check to determine the root cause of the spongy feel.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] User can ask the mechanic to check the brake pads for wear and contamination and provide an estimate for replacement if needed.  
[FACT] User has noticed skipping and hesitation when shifting gears on their bike.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested that the user ask the mechanic to inspect the chain and gears for wear and provide an estimate for replacing the chain if it's worn out.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided details on what to ask the mechanic regarding the chain, including inspecting for wear, checking the chain wear indicator, and inspecting the cassette and chainrings.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended getting a quote for replacing the chain and any other affected components if necessary.  
[FACT] User wants to ensure their tires are properly inflated for the new clipless pedals.
